decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm’s core finishing range with its own product page, management is likely to continue it because it fits the announced automation path and any slow uptake can still be seen as normal market adoption.

Although this UV spot varnishing system is more distant from the established offer, the homepage launch and public Germany-premiere event create visible commitment that makes management inclined to persist rather than withdraw quickly.

This sheet preparation module builds directly on the existing portfolio and supports connected workflow automation, so the firm is likely to retain it and justify further effort as part of a broader system offering.

The B2-format multifinisher was prominently announced on the homepage and is closely aligned with the firm’s strategic direction toward flexible, automated finishing, making withdrawal within a year unlikely.

A hybrid saddle stitcher sits squarely in the firm’s booklet-making core business, so invested sales and service effort plus strategic fit should keep management committed despite limited early evidence.

This folding add-on has lower visibility than some launches, but the cited customer installation gives management a concrete success case and a reason to keep backing it as part of modular automation.
